messages:
Renee T: Help! Went to pick up my blood pressure med and CVS says it's not covered at retail, only via 90-day mail-order. Pharmacist says need a prior auth or exception. I have to start tonight. :sob:

Carlos (People Ops): Ugh. Two paths: 1) provider submits a prior auth (PA) to the carrier, which can take 24-72 hrs, or 2) we can request an expedited pharmacy exception/temporary override so the pharmacy can dispense a 30-day supply while PA processes. Do you have your member ID, Rx number, and the pharmacy's NPI or phone?

Renee T: Member ID: R998776655. Rx#: 987654321 (amlodipine 10mg). Pharmacy says phone 555-204-9911. Pharmacist gave a refusal code: "RET-MDPA" and said they'd accept an employer letter for override in urgent cases.

Maya - Benefits: We can request an expedited override and push the PA with the carrier if you want us to. Fastest: have your prescribing clinic send a PA fax to the carrier with diagnosis and medical necessity and cc benefits@redwood.com. If provider can't fax immediately, email us the Rx label/photo + pharmacist refusal code and we'll request a pharmacy exception same day.

Renee T: Clinic can fax but not until morning. I need something tonight. Is there a company letter that will let the pharmacy dispense now?

Maya - Benefits: We can generate a temporary verification of coverage letter that states active coverage and requests the pharmacy to dispense a one-time 30-day supply pending PA. It won't override carrier rules but pharmacies sometimes accept it for urgent fills. To expedite, please email benefits@redwood.com with subject EXACT: `URGENT RX OVERRIDE - Renee T - Rx 987654321` and attach a photo of the Rx bottle or label and the pharmacist refusal screenshot. We'll create the PDF and also call pharmacy relations for you.

BenefitsBot:  Ticket created: #BEN-5233  "Urgent pharmacy override / PA for retail fill". Expected response: same day for employer letter request; PA submission will be initiated and carrier response time varies. Please attach docs to the ticket.

Pharmacy - WellRx: We received a call from benefits a few minutes ago referencing this ticket. Pharmacist note: if employer letter lists member ID and prescriber contact and the pharmacy files as `Plan Exception - Urgent`, some chains will release a short fill (7-30 days) at pharmacist discretion. Proof of subsequent PA approval required for reimbursement if pay differs.

Carlos (People Ops): FYI med-class note: our plan's formulary requires 90-day mail-order for certain maintenance meds to get lowest copay. But carriers will usually do an override for urgent one-time fills. If you pay OOP tonight and PA is later approved, Benefits will help process a refund/adjustment. Keep receipts and the claim/EOB.

Renee T: Sent email with photo of label and screenshot of refusal code. I'm going to the pharmacy now. Thanks, fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:

Maya - Benefits: Got your email. Generating the temporary coverage/override letter and calling pharmacy relations now. We'll upload the signed PDF to BEN-5233 and also start the PA with the clinic in the morning if needed. If pharmacy still refuses, bring the employer PDF and request a short emergency fill. We'll follow up with refund instructions if you pay.

Renee T: Pharmacy accepted the employer letter and gave me a 30-day supply. Charged $12 copay. You are heroes. I'll upload the receipt to the ticket. :relieved:
